{{Short description|Subset of complex numbers}}
In [[operator theory]], a set <math>X\subseteq\mathbb{C}</math> is said to be a '''spectral set''' for a (possibly [[unbounded linear operator|unbounded]]) linear operator <math>T</math> on a [[Banach space]] if the [[Spectrum of an operator|spectrum]] of <math>T</math> is in <math>X</math> and [[Von Neumann's inequality|von-Neumann's inequality]] holds for <math>T</math> on <math>X</math> - i.e. for all rational functions <math>r(x)</math> with no [[pole (complex analysis)|poles]] on <math>X</math>

:<math>\left\Vert r(T) \right\Vert \leq \left\Vert r \right\Vert_{X} = \sup \left\{\left\vert r(x) \right\vert : x\in X \right\}</math>

This concept is related to the topic of analytic [[functional calculus]] of operators. In general, one wants to get more details about the operators constructed from functions with the original operator as the variable.

For a detailed discussion of spectral sets and von Neumann's inequality, see.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Badea|first1=Catalin|last2=Beckermann|first2=Bernhard|date=2013-02-03|title=Spectral Sets|class=math.FA|eprint=1302.0546}}</ref>
